title: The Andy Razaf tribute album on Period
summary: She discusses the album for Andy Razaf, Leonard Feather's idea, missing tracks in the discography, its low-budget release, and hopes for reissue.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

In the discography, where in fact they do appear on the album. Let's give the titles.

'How Can You Face Me', 'My Fate Is In Your Hands' and 'Massachusetts.'

Well, as a result of the earlier session for Period Records, Leonard got in touch with me and suggested that we do a tribute to Andy Razaf.
As you know, at that particular time, Andy had been ill for quite some time. He was paralyzed from his waist down.
And I don't think --
He had a stroke, I think.
Yeah, he had a stroke.
And I don't think that enough people were aware of some of the things that Andy had done.
So, we got together and Leonard does up most of these things --

To be frank, although I knew about 'Memories Of You' and 'Ain't Misbehaving' and 'Keeping Out of Mischief,' 'Stomping At The Savoy,' 'Honeysuckle Rose,' of course, some of these others -- but I didn't know that Andy had written 'How Can You Face Me.' These were new.
The songs weren't new to me, but the

fact that Andy Razaf had anything to do with them is new to me.
Well you certainly don't hear Stomping At The Savoy as a vocal.
No, you don't.
Certainly not Christopher Columbus.
Chick Webb, I guess, is associated with both of those songs, don't you think?
Yes.
You do, in fact, a little bit more like Ella on those titles than --
Well you'll notice on this album, this is the first chance that I had to get away from 'Loch Lomond' and that type song. And these were things that I wanted to do.
Well, it's a straight ahead swinging album, and I love it. And all I can say is, I wish it was available now.
I like 'Mound Bayou.' You.

And it turns out that Leonard wrote this with Andy. Andy wrote the lyrics, and, of course, Leonard wrote the music.
It's a very good song.
It has the same form as "If I Had A Ribbon Bow."
Yes, it does.
Same verse and sixteen-bar sequence.
I like it very much. Well, we didn't have --
This could've been a very big album for us, but I don't know -- because it was done on such a small label, we had no way of exploiting it in a big way.

And, of course, there wasn't anything wrong with the taping -- I mean with the recording of it. And the material was good enough, but for some reason or other we just didn't get off the ground. We didn't exploit it enough.
Well, that's a -- yes. The business people didn't get off the

Well --
Because I think artistically, it's a tremendous success.
Well Period Records, they were definitely not interested in having anything to do with pop music anyway.

I think Leonard was lucky enough to get these things on Period in the first place, because the Period label was a label that recorded exclusively classical music and did not even distribute in the United States.
So, in order to exploit this album, somebody would've had to take it over, because that's a big enterprise. We certainly weren't in the position to do it.
Where is the company based then.
They had a studio here -- I don't know whether they had a studio here, or whether they just rented a studio for the time being and to make the album. I have no idea.

But we made it, and so far as I know, there were a few albums pressed and that was the end of that.

It was a very low budget-type ent4rprise. I like it because, as I said before, this was an opportunity for me to get away from -- get out of the Loch Lomond and soap mold, and really do something that was currently acceptable to the general listening public.
And I really enjoyed making this album. I was in pretty good voice, I think. The arrangements, although they -- well, Charlie made most of the arrangements -- Charlie Shavers.
As I said before, we always wound up with this little skeletal outlines and played as we went.
But they're the kind of arrangements that if you don't hear it -- if you appear some place and you don't hear that arrangement, it doesn't sound like the same song.
So -- which is very important so far as I'm concerned. I like to sound in person like I sound

I'd like to see this reissued or someone to take over, because although it was made some time ago, I really don't sound that much different. And these are some things that a lot of people never heard me do.
Yeah. Well it's definitely a prime candidate for reissue.
Yeah, right.
